questions.evidenceQuote: In this series of experiments, Zajonc and colleagues showed that repeated exposure amplifies not only familiarity, but also perceived similarity (to the rater) and favorability. Previous research already convincingly demonstrated that perceived similarity leads to attraction. New experiments showed that residential proximity increases both familiarity and perceived similarity, thereby enhancing the interpersonal attractiveness of those around us. These elegant experiments demonstrate that mere exposure increases favorability, providing a compelling causal claim for the Philadelphia marriage study and the Dutch cohabitation study.

specificFindings: The books mechanism summary names familiarity and perceived similarity,not verified identical personality,ancestry or guaranteed marriage. Laboratory/field mechanisms are not treated as retroactively randomising the earlier observational marriage records.

The cities-look-alike question expands possible mere-exposure implications to surroundings. It is a reader-directed rhetorical invitation,not actual user travel history or a survey of every building in every city.

First StatenIsland NewYork large mall impresses through size and store count; later medium PortlandMaine suburban mall puzzles. Maine is not substituted with Oregon and impressions are not turned into objective store-quality tests.

Graduate-school psychology-conference travel is author autobiography. Would fly is past habitual narrative,not a future user booking,actual research random assignment or the author being a professional basketball player.
The repeated airport/suburb/highway/housing/box-store/mall route motivates the environment-similarity question,not identical conference programmes or a claim every city shares the same population.
Tokyo and Osaka share large-city/high-rise/train-station features yet different feels. Perhaps local commercial diversity is a possible explanation,not a separately established sole cause.

Named national chains illustrate recurring familiarity in the books US-suburban description. No current branch-opening verification,consumer recommendation or claim every store on every street is identical is added.
Charlottesville local-cafe daily habit is distinguished from travel-time liking of Starbucks. This is not actual user preference or a universal comparison of coffee quality.
Curt hey is a brief greeting and does not prove fixed dislike of the graduate student. The same Gary at a LasVegas conference receives a warmer response; author,student and setting are not swapped.

Almost hugged is near-action,not a reported completed hug. The candidate and almost hugged him is a continuation; the complete parent supplies its speaker,person and conference context without rewriting original words.

Would I hug in GilmerHall and No chance form a rhetorical contrast with an unfamiliar setting. No chance is conversational emphasis,not a measured all-person zero probability or a request for the user to contact someone.

Mobile states refer to residential turnover,not phones or mobile internet. Nevada/Florida versus Pennsylvania/WestVirginia compare national chain counts; the states were not said to be randomly assigned mobility levels.

If so/should predicts popularity from an idea about familiar stores providing comfort. Sure enough reports the state pattern,also after income/population controls; controls do not prove a unique individual-level comfort mechanism or eliminate every confound.

All three thought conditions show exposure effects but not identical strength. Future-moving imagination produces a stronger familiarity-liking effect than stable-place or typical-day thinking. Participants were not physically moved or guaranteed a future relocation.

Anxiety-related word use covaries with effect strength in the description. In other words gives the authors stress/anxiety interpretation,not a clinical diagnosis or proof stress alone was independently isolated as the sole cause.

Replicable and fun are followed by critical implications. A reliable familiarity effect is not automatically optimal for every choice; the secretary-problem transition asks about the tension with exploring unfamiliar options.

Seriously considering a dozen potential mates is the authors model-based application,not twelve marriages,twelve rejections or a website requirement imposed on the real user. Stressful processes refers to effortful exploration,not a clinical disorder or web navigation.
Bates three other Japanese students explicitly excludes the narrator and names Yoko,Kiyomi,Mariko. It is not the entire Bates population,years in LasVegas or actual user study-abroad history.
The final evidence quote is its exact target count sentence,leaving later unassigned Bates reflections pending. Planned-evidence checks confirm25 new IDs and every published fingerprint retained.

All13 inherited English/Chinese parent pairs were read completely and checked against actual pages113-115,including the repeated-travel narrative,clause continuation,anecdote-versus-study attribution,imagined-versus-actual mobility,statistical controls and complete translations. Unpublished distractors were refined to plausible role,timing,location and scope errors.
